If you're doing PLA/ABS plastics, for example, you'll either need to learn how to design for multiple colors (i.e. splicing colors) or have good ventilation for paints/acrylics. Also, the cheapest 3-D printers have horrible consistency issues when you scale up in size, so creating big batches of a standardized product may be tough. I have helped on a build of 500 or so plastic braille rings, and even then we had a fair amount of variation between them.

I don't mean to sound negative, but I have friends who do this for a living, and I've done a considerable amount of dabbling as well (for clients mainly). To start off, I would definitely start small (in quantity and size) with whatever projects you are working on: few things are worse than making your prototype full-size only to realize that your design is flawed. I'd also recommend that you check out other alternatives (for example, laser cutting or CNC routers) just to see if those might be better suited towards your needs.
